The evidence I found is broader and more structural: control over oil exports, opaque foundations, security-network revenue, and loyalty-based access.","evidence":[{"title":"Iran’s Revolutionary Guards extend control over Tehran’s oil exports, sources say","publisher":"Reuters via Investing.com","date":"2024-12-18","url":"https://www.investing.com/news/commodities-news/irans-revolutionary-guards-extend-control-over-tehrans-oil-exports-sources-say-3778558","summary":"Strong negative evidence: Reuters reported the IRGC controlled up to half of Iran’s oil exports, using shadow fleets and front companies. Since oil revenue funds state spending, this looks like capture of a core state asset by regime-security networks, not separation from office.","question_ids":["7B.4","7B.3","6B.10"]},{"title":"Iran: Freedom in the World 2024 Country Report","publisher":"Freedom House","date":"2024","url":"https://freedomhouse.org/country/iran/freedom-world/2024","summary":"Strong structural negative: Freedom House says corruption is endemic and IRGC/bonyads are above scrutiny, with broad economic power and weak accountability. That is direct evidence of opaque conflicts of interest and privileged access.","question_ids":["7B.4","7B.3","6B.10","7B.1"]},{"title":"Iran's presidential election dominated by Khamenei loyalists","publisher":"Reuters via Investing.com","date":"2024-06-25","url":"https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/irans-presidential-election-dominated-by-khamenei-loyalists-3494879","summary":"Strong negative evidence: Reuters said Khamenei ensured hardline candidates dominated the contest, the Guardian Council approved only five hardliners and one low-profile moderate from 80 applicants, and Khamenei controlled the bulk of financial resources. That is insider filtering and resource control, not clean separation.","question_ids":["7B.4","7B.3","7B.1"]},{"title":"Iran holds presidential vote with limited choices","publisher":"Reuters via Investing.com","date":"2024-06-27","url":"https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/iran-holds-presidential-vote-with-limited-choices-3500514","summary":"Strong negative background: the race was tightly controlled and candidates offered no concrete plans. This supports a patronage-based political economy in which access is managed by regime networks rather than insulated from private gain.","question_ids":["7B.4","7B.3","7B.2"]},{"title":"Factbox: key facts about Iran's elections on Friday","publisher":"Reuters via ThePrint","date":"2024-02-29","url":"https://theprint.in/world/factbox-key-facts-about-irans-elections-on-friday/1983652/","summary":"Strong negative structural evidence: the Assembly of Experts is supposed to choose or dismiss the supreme leader, but candidates must pass Guardian Council vetting. That means oversight is not independent enough to police hidden conflicts or family-linked enrichment.","question_ids":["7B.4","6B.9","7B.3"]},{"title":"Pezeshkian Cabinet: Profiles","publisher":"The Iran Primer / USIP","date":"2024-08-22","url":"https://iranprimer.usip.org/index.php/blog/2024/aug/22/pezeshkian-cabinet-profiles","summary":"Weak positive counter-signal: the cabinet included reformists, hardliners, technocrats, and academics, and the list reportedly had Khamenei, IRGC, and security-agency approval before submission. This suggests some competence-based staffing existed, but it looks compromise-driven and does not show clean separation from patronage politics.","question_ids":["7B.4","7B.3","6B.10"]}]}
